transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I'm here because... well, I feel like I'm always running hot. Like I can't shut the motor off. And lately, that's been getting me in trouble at the firehouse.
During these times when you feel like you can't shut your motor off, have you noticed that you require significantly less sleep than usual to feel rested?
No... I don't think so. I mean, I still need sleep. If I don't get enough, I'm just tired... so, no.
Do you find that you frequently struggle to stay focused on tasks or keep track of your belongings, even when you aren't feeling particularly anxious?
I don't know... I haven't really noticed that. I'm not really an anxious person, so... no, I guess not.
Have you experienced or witnessed any life-threatening events, such as accidents or emergencies at the firehouse, that still cause you to have distressing memories or nightmares?
I mean... it's the job. You see things, sure. But... no. I don't have nightmares about it or anything. I just leave it at work.
Do you find that you need to have a drink to steady your nerves or to help you unwind after a shift?
No. I don't really drink much. Just a beer every now and then, but... not to steady my nerves or anything.
Have you ever had significant trouble with the law or been told by others that you tend to disregard rules or the rights of people around you?
No, definitely not. I mean, I'm a firefighter. I follow the rules. Never had any trouble with the law or anything like that.
Have you experienced any periods, lasting for several days at a time, where you felt unusually 'up,' energetic, or irritable, even if you didn't need less sleep?
No. I don't really get like that. Just... normal energy, I guess. Nothing out of the ordinary.
When you say you feel like your motor won't shut off, do you find yourself constantly worrying about various things, like your job performance, your health, or your family's safety?
No, not really. I don't... I don't sit around worrying about that kind of stuff. It's not like that.
When you have these moments where you feel like your motor won't shut off, do you find yourself becoming easily provoked or aggressive toward others?
No. I'm not an angry guy. It's just... a restless feeling, I guess. I don't take it out on anyone else.
When you have this restless feeling, do you often notice physical sensations like muscle tension, soreness, or feeling physically 'wound up' in your body?
Not really. I mean, I get sore from work sometimes, but... I don't notice anything like that from being restless. It's not a physical tension.
Have you ever been told that you tend to lie, con, or manipulate others for your own personal gain or pleasure?
No. I don't do that.
Do you often feel like there is an empty space inside you, or that you are not quite sure who you are as a person?
No. I know who I am. I don't really get what you mean by an empty space, but... no, I don't feel like that.
When you are in a group or talking with others, do you find that you frequently interrupt people or have a very hard time waiting for your turn to speak?

Yeah, I guess so. Sometimes at the station, if the guys are talking through a plan or something... I just cut in. The answer's already in my head, so I just say it. Then I realize I stepped on somebody's toes or messed up the flow of what they were saying.
Looking back at your time in school as a child, do you remember having similar trouble waiting for your turn to speak or feeling like you couldn't sit still in class?

Yeah... according to my mom, anyway. She says I was like this back in grade school, too. Just... always out of my seat, blurting answers out. 

I guess I lost my homework a lot, and she was always getting notes sent home from the teachers. It wasn't that I couldn't understand it—they always said I was bright enough to do the work. Just... yeah. I guess I've always been like that.
